waveform

waveform is an R package for generating and working with one-dimensional functional data. It provides Gaussian white-noise curves, smoothed Gaussian curves, simple signal shapes, a residual-field smoothness estimate, and tools for evaluating curves on a new grid.

Version: 1.1.0 · Author: Mohammad Reza Seydi

Package website · Function reference

What it can do

  • Generate independent standardized Gaussian white-noise curves.
  • Generate a specified sample size of smoothed Gaussian curves with user-defined mean, standard deviation, and FWHM.
  • Smooth the same noise realization with different FWHM values to compare smoothness directly.
  • Generate Gaussian, square, sine, and cosine signals.
  • Estimate the FWHM of a residual random field.
  • Fit curves with an fda B-spline basis and evaluate them on a denser or sparser grid.
  • Use the included male and female thorax obliquity curves as example data.

Example data

The package includes thorax obliquity curves from 65 male and 71 female participants. Each dataset has 101 evaluation points per participant. See ?male and ?female for details and the source citation.

Install from GitHub

Install the released source directly from GitHub with remotes:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mr-seydi/waveform")

The package imports fda for functional-data fitting in dense_data().

Data layout

Curve matrices use the same orientation throughout the package:

  • Rows are evaluation points.
  • Columns are curves.

Thus gaussian_swn(number_of_curves, num_points) returns a matrix with num_points rows and number_of_curves columns. smooth_gaussian_curves() preserves these dimensions, and dense_data() returns one column per input curve. In the smoothing and curve-generation functions, mu and sig can be scalars or vectors with one value per evaluation point; pointwise vectors are shared across curves.

Functions

Function Purpose Output
gaussian_swn() Generate independent standardized Gaussian white-noise curves. Matrix: points × curves.
smooth_gaussian_curves() Smooth a curve matrix and set its target mean and standard deviation. Matrix with the input dimensions.
gaussian_curves_generator() Generate and smooth curves; calculate pointwise mean and standard deviation across curves. List: curves, mean, and sd.
gaussian_signal() Generate a Gaussian-shaped signal with a specified center, peak, and FWHM. List: signal_values and domain.
square_signal() Generate a piecewise-constant signal over an inclusive interval. Numeric vector.
sin_signal() / cos_signal() Generate periodic signals with adjustable amplitude, frequency, phase, and offset. List: signal_values and domain.
estimate_fwhm() Estimate global FWHM from curves after pointwise centering. Numeric scalar.
dense_data() Fit curves with an fda B-spline basis and evaluate on a new grid. Matrix: evaluation points × curves.

Citation

To cite the package in R, run citation("waveform"). The citation is also provided here in BibTeX format:

@Manual{seydi_waveform_2026,
  title  = {waveform: Simulating One-Dimensional Functional Data},
  author = {Mohammad Reza Seydi},
  year   = {2026},
  note   = {R package, version 1.1.0},
  url    = {https://github.com/mr-seydi/waveform}
}

Development

Source files live in R/, help pages in man/, and tests in tests/testthat/. Long-form guides can be added to vignettes/.

Use devtools::document() to update help pages and devtools::check() to check the package. To manage the project library with renv, initialize it from the package root:

install.packages("renv")
renv::init()
